title: Wiener's lemma
intro: In mathematics, Wiener's lemma is a well-known identity which relates the asymptotic behaviour of the Fourier coefficients of a Borel measure on the circle to its discrete part. This result admits an analogous statement for measures on the real line.

title: Wigner–Eckart theorem
intro: The Wigner–Eckart theorem is a theorem of representation theory and quantum mechanics. It states that matrix elements of spherical tensor operators in the basis of angular momentum eigenstates can be expressed as the product of two factors, one of which is independent of angular momentum orientation, and the other a Clebsch–Gordan coefficient.

title: Wildtype (company)
categories: Biotechnology companies of the United States
Food and drink companies of the United States
intro: Wildtype is an American seafood company that produces cultivated seafood from fish cells. Its headquarters is located in the Dogpatch neighborhood of San Francisco, California and includes a former microbrewery that has been converted into Wildtype's first Fishery where their cultivated seafood is produced.

title: Wiles's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem
resolved_title: Wiles's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem
intro: Wiles's proof of Fermat's Last Theorem is a proof by British mathematician Andrew Wiles of a special case of the modularity theorem for elliptic curves. Together with Ribet's theorem, it provides a proof for Fermat's Last Theorem.

title: Will Young
categories: Alumni of the University of Exeter

People educated at the Arts Educational Schools
intro: William Robert Young (born 20 January 1979) is an English singer, songwriter and actor. He came to prominence after winning the 2002 inaugural series of the ITV talent contest Pop Idol, making him the first winner of the worldwide Idol franchise.

title: William Brocius
categories: Gunslingers of the American Old West
Outlaws of the American Old West
People of the Cochise County conflict
People shot dead by law enforcement officers in Arizona
intro: William "Curly Bill" Brocius (circa 1845 – March 24, 1882), was an American gunslinger, cattle rustler and member of the Cowboy outlaw gang in the Cochise County area of what was then Arizona Territory during the late 1870s and early 1880s. Brocius' name is likely an alias or nickname, and some evidence links him to another outlaw named William "Curly Bill" Bresnaham, who was convicted of an 1878 attempted robbery and murder in El Paso, Texas.

title: William of Soissons
intro: William of Soissons (French: Guillaume de Soissons) was a French logician who lived in Paris in the 12th century. He belonged to a school of logicians called the Parvipontians.

title: Wirtinger's inequality for functions
intro:
For other inequalities named after Wirtinger, see Wirtinger's inequality.
In the mathematical field of analysis, the Wirtinger inequality is an important inequality for functions of a single variable, named after Wilhelm Wirtinger.
